blocks.content: Regional Rural Banks were established to develop the rural economy by providing credit for agriculture, trade, and other rural endeavors.

rows: Rural and semi-urban areas focusing on agriculture and small businesses
Urban, semi-urban, and rural areas catering to general retail and corporate entities
Supervised by NABARD and regulated by RBI
Regulated and supervised directly by RBI
Jointly owned by Union Govt (50%), Sponsor Bank (35%), and State Govt (15%)
Public sector majority ownership or private/foreign shareholders

items: Shareholding ratio of Central Govt : Sponsor Bank : State Govt is 50 : 35 : 15 (a very common exam question).
Prathama Bank was the first Regional Rural Bank in India.
Supervision of RRBs is carried out by NABARD, whereas regulation is under the jurisdiction of the RBI.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) were created on the recommendations of the Narasimham Working Group in 1975.
The first RRB was Prathama Bank, established on October 2, 1975, sponsored by Syndicate Bank.
The equity shareholding of RRBs is distributed among the Central Government (50%), Sponsor Bank (35%), and State Government (15%).
RRBs are regulated by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and supervised by the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD).
